Article Title: Phone numbers, QR code: Punjab BJP's new push to seek public input for 2027 'people's manifesto'
Article Text:
Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon announced three phone numbers and a QR code to collect public suggestions for the party's 2027 Assembly poll manifesto

NEW DELHI: The Punjab BJP on Sunday launched three phone numbers and a QR code to seek suggestions from people across the state for preparing its “people’s manifesto” ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon announced the initiative, saying suggestions from all sections of society would be considered while drafting the manifesto.“We will welcome suggestions from every section and thereafter the poll manifesto will be prepared. It will be a people’s manifesto,” news agency PTI quoted Dhillon as saying.“We have only one agenda, which is Punjab’s progress and development. It will be a manifesto for every Punjabi,” he said.The three phone numbers launched by the party are 07971943333, 9913002027 and 7508560065. People can also scan a QR code to submit their suggestions.Apart from the phone numbers and QR code, the BJP will send vans to villages and cities across Punjab to collect suggestions from people for its manifesto, Dhillon said.The party said the exercise was aimed at gathering inputs from different sections of society before finalising its agenda for the 2027 polls.Dhillon also targeted the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab over law and order, the drug menace, gangsterism and rising debt.Accusing the state government of having “destroyed Punjab” during its tenure, he claimed that the state had fallen behind in development. He also alleged that the AAP government had failed to ensure that funds sent by the Centre reached the people.The Punjab BJP chief further claimed that the state's outstanding debt had nearly doubled under the AAP government, rising from Rs 2.82 lakh crore.
Article Summary: Punjab BJP launches three phone numbers and a QR code to collect public suggestions for the party's 2027 Assembly poll manifesto. Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon says suggestions from all sections of society would be considered while drafting the manifesto.

Article Title: 'Lotus has withered': Akhilesh Yadav's swipe at BJP over 'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' slogan
Article Text:
"Schools that have been shut down will be reopened": Akhilesh Yadav ahead of UP Assembly elections 2027

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Taking a swipe at the BJP over its “Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De” slogan for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav said on Sunday that the slogan itself indicated that the ruling party’s "kamal" (lotus symbol) had withered and needed to bloom once again."'Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De' go ahead and make it bloom. Does it mean the lotus has withered? Why do you (BJP) need to make it bloom again? It has withered," the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister told reporters at a press conference in Lucknow.Akhilesh Yadav also accused the BJP of selectively invoking religious sentiments, clarifying that his party had no objection to religious discourses or 'kathas' but opposed controversial remarks about Hindu deities."The Samajwadi Party is not against 'katha'. But what were the views expressed about the father of Lord Shri Ram, and what was said about Lord Krishna? These are the same BJP people who once made Lord Hanuman dance at their programme," he said, without naming anyone."Can anyone make such remarks about Lord Ram's father? Tell me, what would happen if someone from among us made a similar statement?" he added.Although the SP chief did not name anyone, his remarks appeared to be directed at preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, who recently courted controversy over statements concerning Lord Ram and Lord Krishna.Akhilesh Yadav also hit back at Uttar Pradesh deputy chief minister and BJP leader Keshav Prasad Maurya over his remarks that SP leaders, who once hesitated to chant "Jai Shri Ram", were now uncomfortable with the slogan "Radhe Radhe".Responding to Maurya's comments, Akhilesh Yadav said, "I would never invite him (Maurya) to my house in my lifetime. But you are welcome to visit our house; we will greet you with 'Radhe Radhe'," he told a reporter.The Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to take place in February-March next year. The BJP will be aiming for a third consecutive term in power, while Akhilesh Yadav will look to become chief minister for a second time, having last held the post from 2012 to 2017.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav takes a swipe at the BJP over its “Radhe Radhe Kamal Khila De’ slogan for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections. He says the slogan itself indicated that the ruling party’s "kamal" (lotus symbol) had withered and needed to bloom once again.

Article Title: 'Uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists’: Rahul shares Ardhanareshwar image to target BJP-RSS
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday upped the ante against BJP and RSS , calling them "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" and accusing them of having no understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions."The deeper I go into Indian spiritual and religious traditions, the clearer it becomes," the Congress leader wrote in a social media post on X."The BJP and RSS are uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists with absolutely no understanding of our spiritual and religious traditions," he added.The Congress leader also shared a picture of a sculpture depicting Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in the form of 'Ardhanareshwar'. Ardhanareshwar is a Hindu deity representing Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati in a single form, with one half depicting a male and the other a female.Rahul's remarks come days after he faced criticism over his comments about his parents' relationship at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love'.Recalling his childhood, he said his parents would sit together during meals, with his mother sitting on his father's lap."Now, I thought this was a normal thing. So I would go to my friend's house, but their parents wouldn't be sitting on each other's lap, and I'd ask my friends, 'Guys, what is going on? Why is your mother not sitting on your father's lap?'" he said."... And then we saw it all get smashed. Not just over time - suddenly... We saw one of our anchors (Indira Gandhi) get shot, and then we saw our biggest anchor (Rajiv) get blown to pieces," he added.The remarks drew criticism from BJP leaders, including Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who took a swipe at the Congress leader."Sorry, Ma'am, he couldn't spare you the embarrassment even on such a special day of your life. The nation figured it out long ago. Hopefully you'll see it now too; this product is beyond launching and relaunching," Sarma said in a post on X, sharing a video of Rahul's remarks.The Congress leader countered saying thar fear, anger and hatred had created a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, preventing them from expressing love.He had also shared a photograph of a 12th-century temple sculpture depicting Goddess Parvati sitting on Lord Shiva's lap."As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. Satyam Shivam Sundaram," he had said.Congress had backed Rahul's remarks, saying the Lok Sabha leader of opposition had initiated a much-needed conversation."...Love need not be hidden, affection is not a weakness, and equality begins with treating your partner as an equal," the party had said in a post on X, tagging Rahul's remarks.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi calls BJP and RSS "uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists" He accuses them of having no understanding of India's spiritual and religious traditions. His remarks come days after he faced criticism over his comments about his parents' relationship.

Article Title: 'This is new India's response': BJP takes swipe at Pakistan over its minister's applause at Purana Qila
Article Text:
It highlighted the contrast between the remarks and the Pakistani minister's presence at an event showcasing India's cultural heritage.

The BJP on Sunday took a swipe at Pakistan by sharing a video of Pakistan minister Musadik Malik applauding during the event at the Purana Qila. They shared the moment of Malik applauding at a presentation on Indian civilisation, Kashmir 's culture and the Mahabharata and used it to get back at Pakistan's earlier remarks on Kashmir and India.BJP's national account shared a video montage of Pakistani leaders' statements on Kashmir featuring army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Musadik Malik. Their words are later juxtaposed with visuals of Malik and other delegates applauding at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.The video, edited with the track 'Ari Ari' from Dhurandhar as the background music, was posted by the BJP's national account. It juxtaposed clips of statements about Kashmir, India's water resources and Hindus.It highlighted the contrast between the remarks and the Pakistani minister's presence at an event showcasing India's cultural heritage."Those who lay claim to Kashmir, threaten to break up India and insult Hindus… were applauding India’s civilisation, Kashmir’s culture and the epic of the Mahabharata at the Purana Qila!" the BJP said in its post, adding, "This is the new India’s response!"The video carried captions highlighting remarks such as "Kashmir belongs to Pakistan", "We will cut hands of those who block our water" and "We are different from Hindus.Hindus are inferior". It then showed Malik and other attendees applauding during cultural presentations.The BJP also used captions to underline its political message. One read, "Those who claim Kashmir are applauding when Kashmiri culture is presented as Indian". Another said, "Those who threatened to cut India's hands were left clapping for India".The three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum is being hosted by India at the historic Purana Qila. Malik, Pakistan's minister for climate change and environmental coordination, was among the delegates attending the event.During his address at the forum, Malik had invoked Mughal emperor Humayun and Sher Shah Suri, both associated with the construction of Purana Qila. He described the historic fortress as a reflection of multiple layers of history.
Article Summary: BJP's national account shared a video montage of Pakistani leaders' statements on Kashmir featuring army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and Musadik Malik. Their words are later juxtaposed with visuals of Malik and other delegates applauding at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.

Article Title: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
Article Text:
Amit Shah said migration from 40 villages along the China border has stopped, with population rising amid improved facilities and employment opportunities

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday reached out to Arunachal Pradesh amid protests over a proposed dam project, saying the population in 40 villages bordering China has increased and migration has stopped, citing improved employment, healthcare and other facilities. He made the remarks at a cooperative conference in the state, where he also announced development projects under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme.Shah said the Centre has directed the Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) to procure produce from local cooperatives in border villages instead of sourcing it from cities, strengthening ties between residents and security forces.“I reviewed this yesterday. I am pleased that people have begun returning to all 40 villages (bordering with China), the population there has increased, and migration has stopped. Electricity, employment, and health facilities have been discussed. Water has also been delivered to the hilltops. The Home Ministry has strictly mandated that the ITBP and the Army should not procure their produce from Tezpur or Guwahati; they must be procured from villages and cooperatives,” news agency ANI quoted Shah as saying.“Women in Arunachal Pradesh are supplying dairy products, eggs, vegetables, millets and flour through their cooperatives, bringing prosperity to rural households and transforming local agriculture and strengthening the relationship between villages and the army,” he added.He said employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family should be the key priorities for Arunachal Pradesh's development. He urged cooperative institutions and women's self-help groups (SHGs) to work towards making the state self-reliant in essential food products.“Every cooperative institution and women Self-Help Groups (SHGs) should take up the challenge of making Arunachal Pradesh self-reliant in essential food products. Employment, education, healthcare and the prosperity of every family must be the four key priorities of Arunachal Pradesh's development,” Shah said.He also assured Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister of the Centre's support for development projects, saying the government would open all avenues for the state's progress.“Yesterday, we discussed in detail all the steps of Arunachal's development for about three and a half to four hours, decided the roadmaps for the future, and made some decisions. Kiren Rijiju and I have taken note of things where the central government’s help is needed. I want to assure Pema Khandu and the deputy chief minister that the central government will open all avenues for the development of Arunachal without any delay. Mobile Medical Units were dispatched today to villages in 11 border districts under the Vibrant Village Programme,” he said.Shah also praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's decision to reframe border villages as the country's first villages rather than its last, saying they have the right to development.“Vibrant Village Programme was made for villages in border states. Earlier it was called the country’s last village; Narendra Modi changed the concept and awarded the title of the first village in the country. The biggest right to development is of the border villages of the country,” the Union minister said.Shah on Sunday launched 199 development projects worth Rs 110.95 crore under the Vibrant Villages Programme across 11 border districts of Arunachal Pradesh. He also unveiled the Arunachal Pradesh Cooperative Vision 2047, a blueprint outlining the sector's development over the coming decades.Earlier on Saturday, Shah chaired a high-level review meeting in Itanagar to discuss law and order, internal security, border management and development in Arunachal Pradesh.He also reviewed border security and strategic infrastructure along Arunachal Pradesh's approximately 1,126-km international border with China, given its strategic sensitivity.
Article Summary: Amit Shah said migration from 40 villages along the China border has stopped, with population rising amid improved facilities and employment opportunities. He made the remarks at a cooperative conference in the state, where he also announced development projects under the Centre’s Vibrant Villages Programme.

Article Title: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China’s support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
Article Text:
The US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan

Defence expert says report raises questions for Washington

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Political reactions have poured in after a US congressional commission flagged China’s military support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission said China’s military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict complicated India’s operational planning and tied down its military resources, without Beijing directly entering the fighting.The commission, established by the US Congress in 2000, said China views India as a potential competitor and is working to constrain its rise. It warned that Beijing’s growing military partnership with Pakistan has made a possible two-front conflict a greater concern for New Delhi.“China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India’s rise across multiple domains,” the report said.“May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India’s concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop,” the report added.The assessment by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) has drawn reactions from political leaders, with Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi saying the findings were unsurprising, while Congress leader Shama Mohamed questioned Washington’s own policy towards India and Pakistan.Reacting to the report, Chaturvedi said China had itself acknowledged that Pakistan was using Chinese-supplied equipment and defence systems during the operation.She said successive Indian governments, regardless of political affiliation, had sought to manage national security concerns in their dealings with China, and that the report served as another reminder for India to remain cautious.Chaturvedi said India-China trade ties were important, but warned that the money generated through trade could also be used by Beijing in ways that ran counter to India’s national interests.Congress leader Shama Mohamed said China’s support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor was already known and pointed to unresolved tensions along the India-China border, saying the two countries had not returned to the pre-2020 status quo.Mohamed also questioned the US approach towards India, citing the tariff dispute, pressure over Russian oil purchases and President Donald Trump’s meeting with Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir at the White House.“If the US needs India, it has to work with India and keep Pakistan at a distance,” she said, adding that Washington should take India’s security concerns into account while dealing with the region.She also accused the Indian government of failing to prevent China’s growing presence along the border, including in areas near Arunachal Pradesh.Brigadier Hemant Mahajan (retd) said the report was not a major revelation but raised questions about what Washington knew, what it would do in response and how its claims could be independently verified.Mahajan alleged that Chinese support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor extended beyond supplying weapons and included intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, repairs and technical assistance. He claimed that Chinese satellite capabilities and equipment had been used to support Pakistan’s military preparedness.He also alleged that China had provided Pakistan with substantial military equipment and helped repair platforms that had been out of service before the operation. Mahajan said the support had stopped short of China directly joining the conflict.However, he argued that the performance of Chinese-made weapons during the conflict had raised questions about their effectiveness, and said Indian-made systems had performed better. These assessments were his own.Mahajan further questioned whether the US report would lead to any change in Washington’s policy towards China and Pakistan, saying the broader strategic implications of Beijing’s military assistance extended beyond South Asia.
Article Summary: US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan. Political reactions have poured in after a US congressional commission flagged China’s military support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Priyanka Chaturvedi said the findings were unsurprising, while Congress leader Shama Mohamed questioned Washington's own policy.

Article Title: Karthigai Deepam row: Tamil Nadu govt moves SC against one-time lamp lighting permission atop Thiruparankundram hill
Article Text:
TN govt consults legal experts on SC order allowing one-time Karthigai Deepam lighting at Thirupparankundram hill amid objections from state minister

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its order permitting the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure at Deepathoon.According to news agency ANI, the review petition was filed by the Commissioner of Tamil Nadu's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department.The move comes after the apex court permitted the lighting of the traditional lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time measure.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi on Friday ruled that only authorised representatives of the Devasthanam (temple administration) and government officials would be allowed to visit the site for the ceremony. It also directed the authorities to deploy necessary security, if required.The bench barred members of the public from accessing the site and said no procession, public congregation, slogan-raising or demonstration would be permitted during the ceremony.The top court, however, stayed portions of the judgement that upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at Deepathoon. It clarified that the ceremony would be carried out exclusively by a team authorised by the Devasthanam."The composition and number of such persons shall be settled by the District Collector, Madurai, in consultation with the Temple Executive Officer, the Archaeological Survey of India and the Commissioner of Police, Madurai."The District Collector, Madurai, shall act as the nodal officer for coordination and supervision of the arrangements. The Commissioner of Police, Madurai, shall ensure adequate police protection and regulation of access," the bench said.It further directed the Union of India, through the competent authority, to examine and facilitate the deployment of an appropriate contingent of the Central Reserve Police Force, if required."No member of the general public shall accompany the authorised team to the Deepathoon. No procession, public congregation, demonstration, slogan-raising or activity extraneous to the ceremonial lighting of the lamp shall be permitted at the site. Access to the 'Deepathoon' shall remain confined to the authorised persons and such officials as may be necessary for supervision and security," the bench said.The court directed the district administration to finalise the timing, route of access, duration and other arrangements in consultation with the authorities concerned, keeping in mind public safety, fire prevention, archaeological protection and maintenance of peace."The authorised team shall leave the site immediately upon completion of the ceremony, without leaving behind any temporary article or installation."The Archaeological Survey of India shall prescribe appropriate conditions for the protection and preservation of the monument and its surroundings," it said."The ceremony shall be undertaken strictly in accordance with the applicable statutory requirements. No excavation, construction, structural alteration, permanent installation or damage to any monument, religious structure or property shall be permitted," it added.The top court also clarified that existing religious observances at customary locations would continue without disruption."Equally, the lawful religious activities, access and enjoyment of the dargah and other institutions shall not be interfered with in any manner. The present arrangement shall not confer upon any person an additional right of entry, occupation or control over any portion of the hill," it said.The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya dargah over ownership of the hilltop and the location of the ritual.What is the controversyThe Karthigai Deepam controversy at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Madurai centres on a dispute over where and by whom the ceremonial lamp should be lit on Thiruparankundram hill.For decades, the lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam, near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of the hill.Hindu groups had sought permission to light the lamp at Deepathoon, a stone lamp pillar located higher up the hill, approximately 50 metres from the dargah.The dargah side had told the apex court on Thursday that it owns the entire hilltop of Thiruparankundram and opposed the demand by Hindu worshippers for permission to light the lamp.
Article Summary: The Tamil Nadu government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its order permitting the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure. The review petition was filed by the Commissioner of Tamil Nadu's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi on Friday ruled that only authorised representatives of the Devasthanam and government officials would be allowed to visit the site.

Article Title: Jawan hit by own gun, friendly fire during op to get war pension: SC
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh heard the case

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is not necessary for Army personnel to be hit by an enemy's bullet in order to be entitled to pension under War Injury Element, Supreme Court ruled Friday, ordering that pension be granted even in a case where a soldier is injured in accidental firing from his own gun or his own troops during an operation.A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N K Singh said that the order specifically mentioned that Army personnel would be classified as 'Wounded Battle Casualty' in such cases and the grievously injured soldier would be entitled to the pension.The court said the Army order contemplated two situations: a gunshot or splinter injury suffered 'accidentally', or such an injury caused by firing by own troops. "In either situation, the injury must have been sustained while carrying out operations against the enemy or militants. The present case rests on the first limb, 'sustained accidentally'," SC said."A service weapon may discharge without an intention to cause bodily injury to himself, for example, while holding a weapon, an impact or fall, snagging of the trigger, inadvertent pressure on the trigger, or a mechanical defect... These nature of incidents are clearly distinguishable from the idea of self-inflicted injury, which has a certain element of knowledge or intention so as to disqualify from getting enhanced pensionary benefit," the bench said.SC allowed the plea of Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh who got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K when his weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein. It made him 40% disabled and he was granted an ordinary Disability Element of pension. He sought an enhanced pension under War Injury Element. SC quashed the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes the order of Armed Forces Tribunal, which had rejected his claim. Subedar Major and Honorary Lieutenant Devi Singh got injured in Aug 2002 during Operation Rakshak/Operation Parakram in J&K. His weapon accidentally discharged a bullet that passed through his thigh and damaged the femoral vein.

Article Text:
India, France condemn Pak-sponsored terror attack

NEW DELHI: India and France have condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including crossborder terrorism and violent extremism, and agreed to strengthen cooperation to tackle terror financing, online radicalisation and emerging technological threats.The two countries reiterated their strong condemnation of the April 22, 2025, terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, and the November 2025 terror incident near the Red Fort in New Delhi during the 18th meeting of the India-France Joint Working Group (JWG) on Counter Terrorism held in New Delhi on November 20.According to a ministry of external affairs (MEA) press release, the meeting was co-chaired by Suhel Ajaz Khan, Additional Secretary (Counter Terrorism) in the MEA, and Olivier Caron, French Ambassador-at-Large and Special Envoy for Counter-Terrorism and Organised Crime.During the discussions, both sides exchanged views on the prevailing terror threat in their respective regions and at the global level, including challenges posed by state-sponsored and cross-border terrorism.The two delegations also discussed ways to tackle traditional and emerging security challenges, particularly the misuse of new technologies and financial technologies by terrorist groups.The Indian side briefed the French delegation on its comprehensive National Counter Terrorism Policy and Strategy, PRAHAAR.Both countries also explored ways to deepen bilateral cooperation in combating terrorism through information sharing, capacity-building, training and the exchange of experiences and best practices. They also discussed measures to counter terror financing and online radicalisation.The two sides reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums, including the United Nations, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and the No Money for Terror (NMFT) initiative.The meeting concluded with both sides agreeing to hold the 19th meeting of the Joint Working Group in France on a mutually convenient date.The discussions reaffirmed India and France's commitment to stepping up joint efforts to counter terrorism and address evolving security challenges.
Article Summary: India and France have condemned terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. They agreed to strengthen cooperation to tackle terror financing, online radicalisation and emerging technological threats. Both sides agreed to hold the 19th meeting of the Joint Working Group in France on a mutually convenient date.

Article Title: Murders, kidnappings, extortion: Lawrence Bishnoi aide Goldy Brar on FBI's 10 most wanted fugitive list
Article Text:
FBI adds Goldy Brar to ten Most Wanted Fugitives list over alleged transnational crimes

What the FBI alleges against Goldy Brar

Operation Hardball and US action against crime syndicates

Canada announces separate $250,000 reward

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

FBI warns public not to approach fugitive

The FBI has added Satinderjeet Singh, alias Goldy Brar, to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and announced a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. Brar is accused of being a North American leader of the Lawrence Bishnoi Organised Crime Group (OCG), a transnational criminal network allegedly involved in murders, extortion, drug trafficking and other violent offences across the United States and Canada.The move comes amid a coordinated effort by US and Canadian law enforcement agencies to track down Brar. On November 19, Canada announced a separate reward of up to $250,000 for information leading to his arrest and named him the number-one suspect on the Bolo Program’s new list of the country’s 25 most wanted fugitives.Also read - Canada announces $250,000 reward for Goldy Brar, names him country's most-wanted fugitive According to the FBI, Brar is wanted in connection with multiple federal offences, including racketeering conspiracy, conspiracy to interfere with and attempted interference with commerce by extortion, and conspiracy to distribute and possess controlled substances with intent to distribute. He is also accused of helping direct the activities of the Bishnoi enterprise across several countries.“Satinderjeep Singh, also known as Goldy Brar, is a dangerous individual, and the FBI and our partners have made it our priority to apprehend him, which is why we’re adding him to the FBI’s list of Top Ten fugitives and offering a reward of up to $1 million dollars for his capture,” said FBI Los Angeles Field Office Assistant Director in Charge Patrick Grandy.“The amount of attention this list will bring to his face and description cannot be overstated; his photo will be found on every FBI-affiliated website and social media platform, and will be publicized on every phone around the world until he’s caught.”According to the indictment, Brar was among the trusted lieutenants of Lawrence Bishnoi, who is accused of running a criminal enterprise from prison in India. The indictment alleges that Bishnoi used contraband mobile phones and internet-based communication devices to direct criminal activities, while delegating operational responsibilities to associates, including Brar.The FBI describes the Bishnoi enterprise as a transnational network involved in targeted killings, shootings, kidnappings, extortion, assaults and the trafficking of narcotics and weapons. The group allegedly used violence and online publicity surrounding its criminal activities to create fear and extort victims, particularly in India and among Indian diaspora communities.One of the cases cited in the indictment concerns the killing of a prominent political and religious figure from Punjab who was living in Canada. Identified in court documents as “H.S.N.”, the individual was shot dead by two gunmen as he left a Sikh temple in Surrey, British Columbia, on June 18, 2023.The indictment alleges that Bishnoi and Brar ordered the assassination. The allegations are part of the US federal case against the accused.The indictment also alleges that members of the Bishnoi enterprise stole approximately 520 kg of cocaine from rival drug trafficking gangs in the greater Los Angeles area between March 2024 and July 2025.Brar's addition to the FBI list follows the July 7 announcement of Operation Hardball, a years-long federal investigation into India-based transnational organised crime groups. The US Attorney's Office announced the unsealing of three indictments charging 37 defendants with offences linked to three such groups.The alleged crimes included racketeering, targeted killings, shootings, extortion and the international trafficking of large quantities of narcotics. One of the indictments focused on the Bishnoi enterprise.“The inclusion of this defendant on the FBI’s Top Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list underscores this administration’s determination to bring the full force of the law upon transnational criminal gangs,” said First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli.“Working together with law enforcement in Canada, Europe, and Asia, we will continue to hunt down thugs such as ‘Goldy Brar’ and ensure they never see the outside of a prison again.”At the time of the Operation Hardball announcement, 24 of the federal defendants had been arrested or were already in custody. Authorities said four other fugitives had been captured and one had been confirmed dead. The FBI said it continued to search for five fugitives, including Brar.A day before the latest FBI-related coverage, on November 19, the Winnipeg Police Service announced a reward of up to $250,000 for information leading to Brar's arrest in Canada or the United States. The reward will remain active until November 2, 2027.Brar is wanted under a Canada-wide warrant for first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder in connection with the September 20, 2023, killing of 39-year-old Sukhdool Singh Gill, also known as Sukha Duneke, in Winnipeg.Canadian authorities said arrest warrants were issued on February 23, 2026, for Brar and another suspect, 26-year-old Karanbir Singh, who faces the same charges. Both remain at large.“We will aggressively defend our cities, and our country, against this kind of violence,” said Winnipeg Deputy Chief Cam Mackid in a statement. “We don’t accept it, and we will be relentless.”The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) also welcomed Brar's addition to the FBI's list.“Goldy Brar and his network have wreaked devastating havoc on countless lives—through high-profile murders, shootings, death threats, extortion, arson, and drug trafficking,” said Lisa Moreland, the deputy commissioner of federal policing for the RCMP.“His addition to the FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list speaks to the collective resolve to capture him. The RCMP is committed to continue working with partners in the FBI to bring Goldy Brar to justice.”The FBI has described Brar as extremely violent, armed and dangerous. It said he is known to reside in California and various parts of Canada and warned members of the public against approaching him.Anyone with information about his whereabouts can contact the FBI's toll-free tip line at 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324), approach their local FBI office or the nearest US embassy or consulate, or submit information through the agency's online tip portal. The FBI said tips can be provided anonymously.The case is being investigated by the FBI's Los Angeles Field Office, the Los Angeles Police Department and the RCMP, with assistance from domestic and international law enforcement partners.
Article Summary: FBI has added Satinderjeet Singh, alias Goldy Brar, to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and announced a reward of up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. Brar is accused of being a North American leader of the Lawrence Bishnoi Organised Crime Group (OCG), a transnational criminal network allegedly involved in murders, extortion, drug trafficking and other violent offences.

Article Title: 'Rename Nagpur as Deekshabhoomi': Sanjay Raut's demand amid Dadar Metro renaming row
Article Text:
File photo of Sanjay Raut

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut on Friday demanded that Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar, amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'Chaityabhoomi'.Raut urged chief minister Devendra Fadnavis to bring a proposal to rename Nagpur, saying his party would extend its support even if the move faced opposition."Dadar is just a station. The biggest honour to Dr Ambedkar would be to change Nagpur's name to Deekshabhoomi. The chief minister should bring a proposal and we will support it," Raut told reporters.He said Deekshabhoomi held immense historical significance as the site where Ambedkar embraced Buddhism in October 1956, marking a turning point in the movement against caste discrimination."Social revolution in Dr Ambedkar's life began at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. We will stand by the government on this if any conflict arises on the issue," he added.The demand also found support from the Congress, with legislature party leader Vijay Wadettiwar questioning why Nagpur could not be renamed after the historic site."The name (of Nagpur) should be changed to Deekshabhoomi. What is the problem in changing the name to Deekshabhoomi?" Wadettiwar said.He credited Ambedkar with framing a Constitution that protects India's democracy and said Deekshabhoomi attracts visitors from across the world.The BJP, however, criticised Raut over his demand and accused Shiv Sena (UBT) of opposing the proposed renaming of Dadar Metro station.Maharashtra BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders were using the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) as a proxy to oppose the government's move. He said Raut should first welcome the decision to rename the Metro station as Chaityabhoomi."He (Raut) never goes to Chaityabhoomi, nor does he propagate Dr Ambedkar's thoughts. Such people have no right to speak on the issue," Ban said.Maharashtra minister and senior BJP leader Chandrashekhar Bawankule said Nagpur was already widely associated with Deekshabhoomi."Every person who comes to Nagpur goes to Deekshabhoomi," he said.This comes after Fadnavis announced the state government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station as Chaityabhoomi, subject to completion of the necessary procedures.The announcement had initially caused confusion over whether the proposed name change concerned Dadar railway station. The chief minister's Office subsequently clarified that the proposal applied only to the Metro station and that the suburban railway station would retain its existing name.The renaming proposal has drawn political reactions, with the MNS raising objections to changing Dadar's name.Both Chaityabhoomi and Deekshabhoomi are closely associated with Ambedkar's life and legacy.On October 14, 1956, Ambedkar converted to Buddhism along with hundreds of thousands of followers at Deekshabhoomi in Nagpur. The event became a defining moment in the Dalit Buddhist movement.Ambedkar died on December 6, 1956, and was cremated at Chaityabhoomi in Mumbai's Dadar area.Both sites attract large numbers of followers every year, particularly during Dhammachakra Pravartan Din in Nagpur and Mahaparinirvan Diwas in Mumbai.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena leader Sanjay Raut demands Nagpur be renamed 'Deekshabhoomi' in honour of Dr B R Ambedkar. Demand comes amid row over Maharashtra government's decision to rename Dadar Metro station in Mumbai as 'ChaityabhoomI'

Article Title: 'Sonia Gandhi was real owner of Maruti': BJP's Nishikant Dubey makes big claim; raises questions over '1970 deal'

Article Title: China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor impacted Indian planning: US panel
Article Text:
The US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan

Dragon's playbook

NEW DELHI: A US commission has claimed that China's backing of Pakistan during Operation Sindoor had complicated Indian operational planning and tied down Indian military resources, advancing China's goal of constraining and suppressing India's rise as a peer competitor in the Indo-Pacific region."India is one of the few powers outside the US alliance system with the scale to materially affect the long-term competition with China. China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India's rise across multiple domains," said the latest annual report by US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC). USCC is an independent govt agency created by Congress in 2000 to monitor, probe and submit annual reports on national security and economic implications of bilateral trade and defence ties between US and China. According to the report, China's evolving military partnership with Pakistan has made a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. "May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India's concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop," it said.The USCC report said India’s dependence on Chinese manufacturing has become a key source of leverage for Beijing — and a growing vulnerability for the US.“China has restricted industrial inputs, equipment, technology and expertise to India and required some Indian firms to certify that Chinesesupplied goods would not be reexported to the US. Chinese pricing has also undercut new Indian pharmaceutical production, illustrating Beijing’s intent to undermine Indian suppliers that can compete with established Chinese producers,” it said, adding these dependencies complicate US efforts to diversify supply chains away from China by shifting production to India.It said China’s expanding naval and surveillance presence is beginning to erode India’s longstanding strategic advantages in the Indian Ocean and place additional demands on Indian forces. It said China is beginning to bring its South China Sea playbook to the Indian Ocean, renaming undersea features in ways that could lay the groundwork for potential claims of jurisdiction.
Article Summary: US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan. India is one of the few powers outside the US alliance system with the scale to materially affect the long-term competition with China.

Article Title: Trump, Xi, Putin agree on UN reforms: What it means for India's permanent UNSC seat bid
Article Text:
What was discussed at the trilateral meeting

India's long-standing demand for a seat at the high table

China-Pakistan opposition remains a major hurdle

Is the new agreement a window of opportunity for India?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The world looks very different today from what it did when the United Nations was established in 1945. The global order has shifted from bipolar to increasingly multipolar, relations between countries have changed, and several new nations have emerged while others have ceased to exist.Yet, the exclusive club of five permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has remained unchanged, despite longstanding calls for its expansion to give countries like India a greater say in global affairs.Thursday offered a possible glimpse of change in the global governance system as US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen, bringing together the leaders of three of the five permanent members of the UNSC.While the meeting covered several issues, what stood out was their stated commitment to reforming the United Nations.But could this open a window for India's decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat at the high table, or will the existing power equations continue to stand in its way?Three of the world's most powerful leaders met at a time of deep geopolitical divisions. After around 80 minutes of talks, they emerged with commitments to reform the United Nations, increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, and hold discussions on reducing nuclear risks.According to the joint statement titled "Declaration toward Peace", the three leaders held an in-depth exchange of views on the international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.The first point of the declaration addressed reform of the United Nations."As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, Russia, China and the United States committed to reform the UN so that the UN can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security," the statement read.The agreement has brought New Delhi's longstanding demand for a permanent seat on the Security Council back into focus.However, there is an important distinction. The declaration calls for reform of the UN but stops short of spelling out what those reforms would entail or whether they would include an expansion of the Security Council's permanent membership.That leaves a crucial question unanswered: Are the three powers willing to change the institution's existing power structure, or do they envision reforms that leave their own privileged positions untouched?India, a founding member of the United Nations, has sought a permanent seat on the Security Council for decades. New Delhi's central argument is that a world body created in the aftermath of World War II cannot adequately represent today's world without giving India, the most populous country, a major economy, a leading democracy and a significant contributor to UN peacekeeping operations, a permanent place at the decision-making table.In 1994, India formally announced its candidature for permanent membership at the 49th UN General Assembly and has consistently reiterated its demand since.However, securing a permanent seat is not simply a matter of obtaining support from a majority of countries.Any expansion of the Security Council's permanent membership would require an amendment to the UN Charter under Article 108. This needs approval by a two-thirds majority in the 193-member General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of UN member states, including all five existing permanent members — the US, UK, France, Russia and China.In effect, each of the five permanent members has the power to prevent such an amendment from taking effect, making their consent essential to any expansion.In September this year, external affairs minister S Jaishankar joined his counterparts from Brazil, Germany and Japan, collectively known as the G4, to call for early reform of the Council and expansion in both permanent and non-permanent categories.In a press release, the ministry of external affairs said the G4 ministers emphasised that "it is crucial to implement UNSC reform at the earliest so that the Council is fit-for-purpose, truly reflecting contemporary geopolitical realities.""They underscored that expansion of the UNSC in both the permanent and non-permanent categories of membership is central to such reform and that this position is supported by a majority of member states. In this context, they reiterated the importance of improving the representation of the underrepresented and unrepresented regions and groups, such as Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America and the Caribbean, in both these categories," the statement read.India has also voiced similar concerns through the IBSA grouping with Brazil and South Africa. A joint statement supported "transformative" UNSC reform, permanent seats for India and Brazil, and Africa's aspiration for permanent representation. It also called for a fixed timetable and text-based negotiations during the 81st UN General Assembly.Jaishankar has repeatedly argued that India's exclusion is not merely a setback for New Delhi but also a problem for the credibility of the United Nations itself."To have such a country not there in the key global councils, obviously, it's not good for us, but I would also urge it's not good for the global Council in question," Jaishankar said in 2022.While India has continued to push for a permanent seat on the Security Council, opposition from China and Pakistan remains among the biggest obstacles to its candidature.Beijing has supported Security Council reform in principle but has stopped short of endorsing India's individual candidature.China has maintained that reforms should focus on improving the representation of developing countries, particularly African nations, rather than simply adding a small number of new permanent members.During UN discussions, Chinese representatives have argued that the reform process should not be reduced to the individual aspirations of countries seeking permanent membership.In November 2022, China's then Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Zhang Jun, opposed the adoption of a negotiating text or a timetable for UNSC reform. He warned that such a move could lead to "conflicts" and even "derail the process".Zhang also criticised countries seeking permanent membership to enhance their international standing, in remarks widely seen as an indirect reference to India and the G4."Some countries had their own agenda for reforms, seeking permanent membership to enhance their international standing," he said.Pakistan, meanwhile, is a leading member of the Uniting for Consensus group, also known as the Coffee Club, which opposes the creation of new permanent seats and favours expanding the elected, non-permanent category of membership.Unlike China, Pakistan is not a permanent member and cannot independently block an amendment to the UN Charter through the ratification requirement. However, it can oppose India's candidature through diplomatic negotiations and coalition-building within the General Assembly.The two countries' positions, along with differences among the existing permanent members, have complicated efforts to reach an agreement on the future composition of the Security Council.Speaking to The Times of India, Jawaharlal Nehru University professor Rajan Kumar described the recent summit between the three leaders as more of a diplomatic gesture than a serious commitment to concrete changes in the global governance system."It is a major development that the three countries have met to discuss UN reform, but I believe it is more of a lip service than a serious commitment towards taking any concrete steps towards oil supply chain, nuclear disarmament, reform in the global governance system," he said.Kumar argued that despite agreeing on the need for reforms, the three countries have little common ground when it comes to changing the existing power structure of the Security Council.According to him, their competing geopolitical interests make it difficult to expect a consensus on expanding permanent membership, particularly when the existing arrangement gives them considerable influence over international decision-making."All three countries are opposed to expanding the UNSC. Moreover, the US, Russia and China often use their veto power against each other on issues at the Security Council. When the US raises an issue, China and Russia often align against it, and vice versa. So, do you really expect them to reach a consensus on expanding the UNSC to accommodate countries like Brazil and India?" he asked.The concern is that while the three countries may agree on the broad need to make the United Nations more effective, they have little incentive to support changes that could dilute their own influence.The Shenzhen declaration has certainly brought the question of UN reform back into the conversation. However, without a specific proposal for Security Council expansion or a commitment from the permanent members to support it, there is little to suggest that the existing power structure is about to change.For India, the agreement may offer a glimmer of hope, but its decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat remains a distant prospect.The three powers have agreed that the United Nations needs reform. Whether they are willing to share the power that comes with permanent membership is an entirely different question.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen. The meeting covered several issues, but what stood out was their stated commitment to reforming the United Nations. Could this open a window for India's decades-long ambition of securing a permanent seat at the high table?

Article Title: Prove you're alive with a selfie: What pensioners need to know about Jeevan Pramaan
Article Text:
The Digital Life Certificate system in India provides a hassle-free way for pensioners to verify their identities annually through a simple selfie

What is a Digital Life Certificate and why pensioners need it

How a selfie-based Digital Life Certificate works

Who can use this facility and when must they submit it

What can go wrong

What if face authentication fails

Is the digital system safe? What pensioners should keep in mind

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Imagine having to prove every year that you are alive to keep receiving your pension. For millions of India's pensioners, that routine may now take little more than a selfie. No bank visit, no long queues and no need to depend on someone else to submit a life certificate.A smartphone camera can now do the job. Through the government's Jeevan Pramaan system, pensioners can use Aadhaar-based face authentication to verify their identity and generate a Digital Life Certificate (DLC) from home.The system captures their live facial image and matches it with the photograph linked to their Aadhaar number, allowing the certificate to be sent electronically to the pension disbursing authority.The facility is particularly significant for elderly, sick and differently abled pensioners, for whom travelling to a bank or pension office can be difficult.The government is now pushing wider adoption of the technology through its fifth nationwide Digital Life Certificate campaign, running from November 1 to 30, 2026, with a target of 2.30 crore certificates, including 1.50 crore through face authentication.A Digital Life Certificate is an electronic document that confirms a pensioner is alive and eligible to continue receiving pension payments.Government pensioners are required to submit this certificate periodically to the authority responsible for disbursing their pension. The requirement is intended to ensure that pension payments continue to reach eligible beneficiaries and are not credited after a pensioner's death.Under the traditional system, pensioners generally had to appear before their bank or another authorised official to establish that they were alive. The certificate was then submitted to the pension disbursing agency for processing.For elderly pensioners, particularly those suffering from illness or mobility problems, travelling to a bank or government office every year could be difficult.The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in a December 2014 circular to banks, acknowledged that several pensioners found it difficult to submit life certificates on time despite the facility being available at different branches of their pension disbursing banks.To address this problem, the government launched Jeevan Pramaan on November 10, 2014, introducing an Aadhaar-based Digital Life Certificate system. Developed by the then department of electronics and information technology, the initiative aimed to remove the need for pensioners to physically visit their pension disbursing authorities to submit the certificate.The official Jeevan Pramaan portal describes the initiative as a way to address the "hardship and unnecessary inconvenience" faced by elderly and infirm pensioners who may be unable to appear personally before the authorities.Under the system, a certificate generated after successful biometric authentication is stored in a central repository and made available electronically to the pension disbursing agency.The process is more than simply clicking a selfie and uploading it. It uses Aadhaar-based facial authentication to verify the pensioner's identity before generating the certificate.The technology was introduced to make the process easier, particularly for elderly pensioners whose fingerprints may have become difficult to capture with age.To use the facility, pensioners need two applications on their smartphones, the government's Jeevan Pramaan app and UIDAI's AadhaarFaceRD app.The latter enables the phone camera to capture the pensioner's face for authentication. The official Jeevan Pramaan portal says that a separate fingerprint or iris-scanning device is not required for face authentication.The process begins with the pensioner entering details such as Aadhaar number, name, mobile number and pension-related information, including the Pension Payment Order (PPO) number, bank account and pension disbursing authority.The user then completes the required operator authentication, which is a one-time process and can also be performed by the pensioner. After providing consent, the pensioner captures a live facial image using the smartphone camera.But how does the phone know that the person in front of the camera is the actual pensioner? The captured image is sent for Aadhaar-based face authentication, where UIDAI matches it with the facial photograph linked to the Aadhaar number provided.UIDAI describes this as a 1:1 matching process, meaning the live image is checked against the photograph associated with that particular Aadhaar number, rather than being searched against a database of millions of faces. The authority also says face authentication is based on the Aadhaar holder's consent.Once authentication is successful, the Digital Life Certificate is generated with a unique identification number called the Pramaan ID.An acknowledgement is sent to the pensioner's registered mobile number, while the certificate is stored in the Jeevan Pramaan repository and made available electronically to the pension disbursing agency. This means the pensioner does not ordinarily need to visit the bank to submit a printed copy.The Jeevan Pramaan facility is available to pensioners whose Pension Sanctioning Authority (PSA) is registered on the platform. This includes eligible pensioners receiving pensions from Central and state governments and other government organisations.The facility is also available to eligible Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS-95) pensioners, provided their pension disbursing agency is onboarded on the system.For Central government pensioners, submitting an annual life certificate in November is necessary for the continuation of pension payments.However, pensioners aged 80 and above are given an additional window and can submit their certificates from October 1 every year. The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare reiterated these rules in an office memorandum dated October 26, 2026.Importantly, not every pensioner follows the same submission schedule. For instance, EPS-95 pensioners can submit their life certificates at any time during the year, with the next certificate remaining valid for one year from the date of the previous submission.Therefore, the November deadline applicable to Central government pensioners should not be treated as a universal deadline for all pension categories.There are also certain restrictions. According to the official Jeevan Pramaan FAQ, pensioners who have been re-employed or remarried are not eligible to use the Digital Life Certificate facility and must submit their life certificates through conventional methods.While the Digital Life Certificate system is designed to make pension verification easier, generating the certificate does not necessarily mean that the process is complete.A pensioner's face may be successfully authenticated and a certificate generated, but errors in pension details or the selection of the wrong pension disbursing authority can prevent it from being updated in the bank's records.This problem was highlighted at the 35th meeting of the Standing Committee of Voluntary Agencies (SCOVA), held on March 10, 2026, under the department of pension and pensioners' welfare.The meeting discussed complaints of delays and rejection of Digital Life Certificates submitted through Jeevan Pramaan, particularly involving Bank of Baroda and Central Bank of India.Central Bank of India disclosed that during the government's November 2025 Digital Life Certificate campaign, 79,905 certificates belonging to its pension account holders were uploaded to the Jeevan Pramaan portal. Of these, 60,637 were successfully updated in the bank's pension processing system, while the remaining 19,268 were rejected.This means around 24 per cent of the certificates uploaded to the portal were not updated in the bank's records.The bank attributed the rejections mainly to pensioners entering incorrect pension account details. It also pointed to cases involving defence and telecom pensioners who had moved to the SPARSH and SAMPANN pension systems respectively but continued selecting Central Bank of India as their pension disbursing agency while submitting their certificates.Bank of Baroda identified similar problems, including incorrect PPO numbers, account numbers and selection of the wrong Pension Sanctioning Authority. It also reported cases in which pensioners submitted certificates through both physical and digital modes or generated multiple digital certificates, leading to processing complications.The distinction is important for pensioners: successful face authentication confirms identity, but the certificate must also reach the correct pension authority and be updated in its records. Pensioners should therefore retain their Pramaan ID and check the certificate's status rather than assuming that a successful scan automatically completes the process.Face authentication may not work every time. Poor lighting, incorrect positioning of the face, slow internet connectivity or incorrect pension details can prevent the certificate from being generated.The Controller General of Defence Accounts (CGDA), in its guidance on Digital Life Certificates, has also identified locked Aadhaar biometrics, an incorrect PPO number, an unclear facial image and failure to follow the app's instructions during the scan as possible reasons for unsuccessful submissions.If a pensioner receives an SMS informing them that their Digital Life Certificate has been rejected, the Jeevan Pramaan portal advises them to contact their Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA), such as their bank or post office.The pensioner should verify the details entered during submission and generate a fresh certificate with the correct information and biometric authentication. The status of the certificate can also be checked by downloading it from the official Jeevan Pramaan portal using the Pramaan ID.For pensioners who do not own a smartphone or are unable to complete the face scan, the digital system is not the only option. They can visit a bank branch, post office or authorised Common Service Centre (CSC) to submit their life certificate through available biometric facilities.Banks also offer doorstep banking services through which an agent can visit the pensioner's home to complete the process.India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) also provides a doorstep Digital Life Certificate facility through postmen and Gramin Dak Sevaks.Under the service, an authorised postal representative visits the pensioner's home and completes the authentication process using the available biometric facility.The standard IPPB service is charged at Rs 70, inclusive of applicable taxes, for successful certificate generation. However, eligible EPS-95 pensioners can avail the separate EPFO-IPPB doorstep facility free of charge.Importantly, submitting a Digital Life Certificate is an additional facility and not a compulsory replacement for the traditional method.Pensioners who prefer physical submission can continue to provide their life certificates through the authorised conventional channels. The State Bank of India also confirms that physical life certificates will continue to be accepted from pensioners who prefer this method.Since the process involves Aadhaar-based biometric authentication, consent and data protection are important considerations.The Jeevan Pramaan application requires pensioners to provide consent before their Aadhaar details and biometric information are used for authentication.According to the consent declaration displayed in the application, the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC) state that the pensioner's biometric will not be stored or shared.Pensioners should download the Jeevan Pramaan and AadhaarFaceRD applications only through official app stores and avoid sharing their Aadhaar details, OTPs or banking information with unknown callers or agents. They should also retain the SMS acknowledgement and unique Pramaan ID generated after successful authentication.The government describes Jeevan Pramaan as an additional facility alongside existing methods of submitting life certificates. Its purpose is to make an essential annual requirement less burdensome for pensioners, particularly those who are elderly or unable to travel.However, the process does not end with a successful face scan. Pensioners must ensure that their certificate is correctly generated, reaches the appropriate pension disbursing authority and is accepted in the pension records.
Article Summary: Digital Life Certificate system in India provides a hassle-free way for pensioners to verify their identities annually through a simple selfie. The government is pushing wider adoption of the technology through its fifth nationwide Digital Life Certificate campaign, running from November 1 to 30, 2026. To use the facility, pensioners need two applications on their smartphones.

NEW DELHI: Venue of the first civilisational dialogue under the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Forum, Purana Qila symbolised civilisational continuity but in the case of Pakistan with a different perspective. In marked contrast to India, which It’s minister Musadik Masood Malik on Saturday chose to emphasise that the foundations of the Old Fort were laid by Humanyun whose origins lay in central Asia and that its construction was carried forward by Sher Shah Suri who came from Afghanistan as he sought to focus on the sub continent’s cultural diversity.“Its foundation was laid by Humayun, who belonged to the Timurid dynasty and had arrived from Central Asia. Its construction was further carried forward by Sher Shah Suri, who came from Afghanistan. Thus, within a single wall, one could find the art of two different rulers, two cultural layers, and traces of two traditions,” Malik said.India has touted Old Fort as the perfect venue for the meet with its multi-layered history and its identity as the ancient city of Indraprastha mentioned in the epic ‘Mahabharata’. As part of the retelling of the approximately 3000-year long history of the site, India showcased nine layers of continuity--among them the standing ramparts built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, around 1533 CE.Reflecting on the excavations at the site, Malik said, “Delhi has not been diminished by civilisations and people coming from outside; rather, it has grown stronger”.During his inaugural speech on Friday Prime Minister Narendra Modi had also reflected on the history of Purana Qila to assert India’s civilisational journey going back thousands of years to the Mahabharata period. He also visited the ‘Mahabharata Pavillion - Anant: A rare 18th century Mahabharata scroll’ and the exhibition ‘Astitva’ offering an immersive account of Delhi’s history through archaeological evidence, that have been curated for the leaders from SCO countries to see.Day two of the Fourm saw ministers of all participating nations make statements. Malik who happens to be the Climate Change and Environmental Coordination referring to archaeological remains from different periods discovered during excavations at Purana Qila, said that the fort in which the delegates were seated was, in itself, a story. He appreciated the description of the event as ‘Tehzeeb Ki Guftagu’, or ‘Dialogue of Civilisations’.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik expressed a desire to visit some of India's heritage sites, including the iconic Taj Mahal . Malik attended the SCO meeting in New Delhi as part of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government.His visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India since then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's high-profile visit in 2023 for the SCO meeting.Accompanied by his wife and a senior Pakistani official, Malik spoke about his interest in exploring India beyond the multilateral engagement. Both are visiting India for the first time.Asked whether he planned to visit the Taj Mahal and explore other parts of the country, Malik said he hoped to meet people and see some places if his schedule allowed."I have come to India for a few days. Tomorrow I will be engaged due to the SCO forum. I may not be able to explore much this time, but whatever opportunity I will get, I will try to meet people also and see some places, and understand them. People are the same everywhere," he said.The Centre, meanwhile, denied imposing any restrictions on the movement of Malik or other ministers attending the event. Official sources said all visiting ministers were free to travel anywhere in the country, including the Taj Mahal and Humayun's Tomb.However, security considerations may have affected the possibility of Malik visiting the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah.Speaking on the sidelines of the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the historic Purana Qila, Malik was also asked whether the multilateral engagement could help improve India-Pakistan relations He said he had come to India for discussions in a multilateral context, while underlining the importance of cultural exchanges in bringing people and countries closer."This forum is itself multilateral. You should engage in multilateral discussions. Even the questions you have asked today have not been bilateral; everything here is happening in a multilateral context. We have also come here for multilateral discussions," he said.Amid continued unease in bilateral ties following the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam terror attack , which claimed 26 lives, Malik said culture had a "key role" to play in fostering dialogue between the two countries.He stressed that cultural engagement was not limited to bilateral relations but had wider regional significance, adding that greater understanding between people was essential for the region's progress."Unless we understand each other, our way of thinking and manners of living, we won't be able to grow. Through dialogues, we will get each other's perspectives and get to know each other's understanding, and that's how the region will be able to grow," the Pakistan minister said.India-Pakistan ties deteriorated further in April 2025 after Pakistan-backed terrorists killed 26 people in an attack in south Kashmir's Pahalgam. India responded by launching counterterror Operation Sindoor , a military operation targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir.India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty in 2025 following the Pahalgam attack, among a series of measures taken against Pakistan.
Article Summary: Pakistan's minister Musadik Malik expressed a desire to visit some of India's heritage sites. Malik attended the SCO meeting in New Delhi as part of the Shehbaz Sharif-led government. Article Title: Over 10k postgraduate medical seats in blocked category; govt may review float system
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: More than 10,000 postgraduate medical seats were listed under the blocked category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling, with the data indicating that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously, prompting the govt to consider changes to the newly introduced float system.According to the SARTHA app, a medical admission and counselling platform for NEET-PG and NEET-UG aspirants, 10,105 seats were listed under the 'Blocking' category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. The app, filtered for MCC (All India) counselling, describes these as seats held by students who also have an allotment in another counselling process. The data was shared by Dr Kapil Dev on social media.The branch-wise breakup showed MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026, followed by MS Obstetrics and Gynaecology (861) and MS General Surgery (786), according to the app. Dr Nachiket Bhatia, a medico-socio activist, has also flagged the issue on his social media account.A senior official familiar with the counselling process said the float facility, which allows candidates to retain an allotted seat while seeking an upgrade, could be contributing to dual seat blocking as all-India and state counselling run parallelly on separate platforms. "A candidate may opt for float in both processes and end up blocking two seats," the official said.Introduced for students' convenience, the facility allows candidates to retain seats while seeking an upgrade, with physical joining becoming compulsory in the third round. The official said govt may consider restricting float to the first round and making physical joining compulsory from the second round in future counselling cycles. "This is the first time we have introduced the float system in this manner.We will analyse the situation after the third round."The official also flagged the absence of a common counselling platform linking all-India and state processes, which run simultaneously on separate portals, making it difficult to track candidates holding seats in both. A common portal could prevent multiple allotments, but differences in state reservation policies and concerns over loss of control have hindered integration.Meanwhile, Federation of All India Medical Association has sought a 24-hour deferment of NEET-PG Round 2 results and a one-day window for eligible candidates to surrender either their All India or state quota seats.
Article Summary: 10,105 seats were listed under the ‘Blocking’ category after Round 2 of NEET-PG 2026 counselling. Data indicated that some candidates were holding one seat through All India counselling and another through state counselling simultaneously. MD General Medicine accounting for the highest number of blocked seats at 1,026.

Article Title: Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren writes to CJI seeking urgent appointment of HC chief justice successor
Article Text:
Soren said prolonged interim arrangements could create uncertainty

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren wrote a letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium, urging them to expedite the appointment of a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.In his letter to the CJI and Collegium members, Soren warned that the absence of a permanent successor could lead to another interim arrangement, affecting administrative continuity and institutional planning in the high court, as cited by PTI.“Without the Collegium's immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement… I hope it (the Collegium) will not disagree with me that the office of the Chief Justice is central to the administrative and judicial functioning of a high court,” he wrote.Soren also stressed the need for stable judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the justice delivery system, saying frequent leadership transitions could disrupt the functioning of the institution.
Article Summary: Hemant Soren wrote a letter to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and the Supreme Court Collegium. He urged them to expedite the appointment of a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M S Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.
