Article Title: 'Working to suppress India’s rise': US panel report flags China's support to Pakistan during Operation Sindoor
Article Text:
The US panel report says China is using military, maritime and economic pressure to constrain India's rise, while strengthening its support for Pakistan

What report said on China suppressing India's rise

China-Pakistan military partnership

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

China’s military support to Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict added to New Delhi’s security challenges and raised concerns about a possible two-front threat, a US congressional commission report has said. The report said Beijing has been working across military, economic and maritime domains to constrain India’s rise as a strategic power.The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in its report on China’s efforts to expand global power and influence, said the conflict following Operation Sindoor highlighted how Beijing could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without directly entering the fighting.According to the report, Pakistan used advanced weaponry procured from China during the fighting. It also said China reportedly increased pressure on India by deploying a survey vessel with advanced sensors around waters within India's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) as tensions escalated.The report further noted that military officials in India had claimed after the conflict that Pakistan may have received real-time satellite imagery or other intelligence support from Beijing.China neither confirmed nor overtly denied the claim, it said.In May 2026, China's state-run CCTV aired an interview with Zhang Heng, an engineer from the Aviation Industry Corporation (AVIC) of China's Chengdu Aircraft Design and Research Institute, a key developer of fighter aircraft and uncrewed autonomous vehicles. Zhang confirmed that he and other Chinese AVIC personnel provided onsite technical support in Pakistan during the May 2025 conflict, the report said.The report said India’s size, military strength and strategic location make it a significant factor in the long-term competition with China. It noted that India is the world’s most populous country and largest democracy, and shares a 2,100-mile contested border with China. Its position along key sea lanes in the Indian Ocean also gives it strategic importance.“China understands this, and it is actively working to suppress India’s rise across multiple domains,” the report said.It said Beijing was continuing its military buildup, asserting sovereignty claims along the disputed border, deepening military support for Pakistan and expanding its naval and surveillance presence in the Indian Ocean.The report described China's economic leverage as its “sharpest tool”. It said Beijing was “using its control over critical industrial inputs, technology, and expertise to preserve its manufacturing advantages and make it harder for India to build competing capacity”.Citing examples, the report said China had “restricted exports of key inputs and products to India to exert economic pressure”, “recalled engineers and withheld equipment to slow India’s electronics manufacturing”, and “slashed pharmaceutical input prices to undercut new Indian plants”. It also said Beijing had imposed export controls on battery technology to impede the development of India's clean energy industry.The report further flagged China's move in 2025 to require Indian firms to certify that certain Chinese-supplied inputs would not be re-exported to the US. While Beijing suspended the requirement as part of the broader Trump-Xi trade détente, the report said it remained “a lever that can turn India’s dependence on China into a weapon aimed at U.S. supply chains”.The report said China's growing military partnership with Pakistan has made the possibility of a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. Beijing has deepened its ties with Islamabad since the 1962 Sino-Indian war, with cooperation spanning defence, infrastructure and economic sectors."China’s evolving military partnership with Pakistan has made a two-front contingency an increasingly critical concern for India. The May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without Beijing entering the fighting directly, adding to India’s concerns about how a future conflict with Pakistan could develop," it said.China is Pakistan's main defence supplier, accounting for 81% of its arms imports between 2020 and 2024, the report said.It added that China's military support to Pakistan has magnified the strategic challenges India faces in its longstanding rivalry with Islamabad, raising concerns that a conflict with one could escalate into a challenge involving both.
Article Summary: China's military support to Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict raised concerns about a possible two-front threat, a US congressional commission report has said. The report said Beijing has been working across military, economic and maritime domains to constrain India's rise as a strategic power.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Saturday questioned the BJP-led Bihar government's decision to name the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge after JD(U) leader and former CM Nitish Kumar instead of the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh.In a post on X, Khera criticised the move, alleging that the manner in which the renaming was being carried out hurt the sentiments of the Sikh community. He also questioned whether Nitish Kumar was being pushed out of the political mainstream by the BJP."The bridge that had been decided to be named after the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh Ji, is now being decided to be named after Nitish Kumar Ji. Why is this being done in a way that tramples on the sentiments of the Sikh community? Doing in his lifetime what should be done after his death also raises the question: Why is Nitish Kumar Ji being pushed out of the political mainstream in such a hurry?" he asked.Khera also shared an official document issued by Bihar's Road Construction Department, which contained a noting on a non-official resolution moved by RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav Separately, Tejashwi accused the BJP-led Centre of attempting to take credit for the bridge project, claiming that the party had made no contribution to its construction.In a video message, the RJD leader questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's scheduled visit to dedicate the bridge to the nation, alleging that the project had already been inaugurated by Nitish Kumar and had been operational for 17 months."Prime Minister, before coming to Bihar today, you should stand before a mirror and take a good look at yourself: why is there not even a speck or a penny’s worth of your contribution to the bridge in Bihar whose ribbon you are coming to cut? Prime Minister, please repeat all the promises and lies you made to Bihar today. Will you?," said Tejashwi.He further claimed that the bridge had been inaugurated by Nitish Kumar 17 months ago and questioned the Centre's role in the project."This bridge was inaugurated 1 year and 5 months ago by the then Chief Minister, Shri Nitish Kumar. This bridge has been in use for the past 17 months, and hundreds of thousands of vehicles have crossed it over the past 1 year and 5 months. Are you inaugurating it again so that your name can also be written on the plaque, even though the central government has had absolutely no involvement in it? According to the Bihar government, this bridge was to be named either after the freedom fighter, the late Shri Akshayvat Rai, or after the tenth Guru, Guru Gobind Singh, because it is located near the birthplace of this revered Guru. It comprises a 9.7-km main bridge and 10 km of approach roads.The bridge will provide an additional crossing over the Ganga, easing traffic pressure on the existing Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu and reducing travel time between north and south Bihar.It is also expected to improve connectivity for residents of Raghopur Diara, providing better access to Patna and essential services such as healthcare and education.The project is expected to facilitate the movement of agricultural produce and industrial goods, improve access to markets and boost trade and commerce across the region.
Article Summary: Congress leader Pawan Khera questions decision to name Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur bridge after JD(U) leader and former CM Nitish Kumar instead of the tenth Sikh Guru, Guru Gobind Singh. PM Narendra Modi scheduled to dedicate the Nitish Setu, an extradosed cable-stayed bridge over the Ganga, to the nation.

NEW DELHI: The selection of India's playing XI has triggered a face-off between the Congress and the BJP, with the opposition alleging discrimination against pacer Mohammed Siraj and the ruling party accusing it of dragging communal politics into cricket.The exchange began after India’s team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj against New Zealand, despite the Hyderabad pacer’s impressive record and reputation for delivering in challenging conditions.Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Siraj’s exclusion, suggesting that his religious identity could have played a role in the decision."His name is Siraj -- isn't that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason behind it? Congress now does vote bank politics even in Cricket team selection! Congress says - 'Siraj was left out because he was a Muslim'."Pointing out that all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja had also been left out, Bhandari said, "Every cricketer wears the jersey representing India! Stop dividing Indian cricket team for vote bank and communal politics!"Siraj's omission has also drawn attention because of the role he has played in India's pace attack over the past few years.Fifteen months ago, on a cloudy morning in London, Siraj stepped out of Jasprit Bumrah's shadow to produce one of the most memorable performances of his career. The pacer emptied the tank on the final day of a gruelling five-Test series to help India secure a 2-2 draw against England at The Oval.His performance appeared to signal the beginning of a new phase in his career, with Siraj emerging as a potential leader of India's pace attack as Bumrah entered an intensive workload management programme.However, the pacer was left out on Thursday despite conditions in Wellington appearing tailor-made for seam bowling. The team management instead went ahead with four other seamers.One possible reason for the decision could be Siraj's recent form. His underwhelming performance against Sri Lanka in the Colombo Test three months ago may have prompted the team management to reassess his place in the playing XI.
Article Summary: Mohammed Siraj left out of India's pace attack against New Zealand. Congress alleges discrimination, BJP says stop dividing team for vote bank and communal politics. India's team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj.

Article Title: Humayun, Sher Shah and ‘one fort’: Pakistan minister highlights Purana Quila’s layered history at SCO forum

The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.

Three-day SCO civilisational forum at Purana Quila

NEW DELHI: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik invoked Mughal emperor Humayun and Afghan ruler Sher Shah Suri while addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Delhi's historic Purana Quila on Saturday. Referring to the fort's layered history, Malik said it reflected how two rival rulers had contributed to the construction of the same monument.Speaking at the thematic session titled 'Civilisational and Cultural Expressions', chaired by Union culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Malik described Purana Quila as a symbol of multiple historical influences."This (Purana) Quila, where we are sitting, is in itself a story. A fort, whose foundation was laid by Humayun, who had a descent from the Timurid (dynasty) linkage.. came from Central Asia. And Sher Shah Suri further built on it, who was an Afghan. One wall, two rivals, meaning two rulers and one fort, meaning two layers and one trench," the Pakistan minister said.Malik also shared a video of his address on X and wrote in Urdu that the Quila is a "story".He further emphasised the importance of dialogue between different identities and cultures, saying, "dialogue is between distinct identities, and between diversity, and, we have come here for that dialogue only"."Meaning, many voices, many identities, and their dialogues, and free flow of ideas, among them... free flow of identities. The wisdom lies in it, the wisdom lies in embracing it, embellishing it. So, wisdom is there in it, and needs courage too. And, we have gathered here to celebrate these two things," he added.The remarks come amid strained India-Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack. Malik is visiting India for the first time.India is hosting the three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Purana Quila to highlight the country's rich civilisational heritage and the layers of history spanning thousands of years.Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the summit on Friday evening in the presence of delegates from SCO member countries, including Malik.The choice of venue also draws attention to the fort's historical significance. Humayun, the second Mughal emperor, laid its foundation, while Sher Shah Suri later expanded it. Humayun's Tomb, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi's Nizamuddin area, is also located nearby.The tomb is the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent. It marked a major departure from earlier funerary traditions and is considered a pioneering example of Indo-Islamic architecture, according to the culture ministry.As part of the forum, a special exhibition titled 'Astitva: The Essence of our Existence' has been organised for SCO delegates. It offers an account of Delhi's history through archaeological evidence dating from 1,200 BC to 1200 CE. The exhibition includes excavated remains, artefacts, architectural fragments and other significant discoveries.
Article Summary: Pakistan minister Musadik Malik is visiting India for the first time. He is addressing the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum at Delhi's historic Purana Quila. The remarks come amid strained India- Pakistan relations following the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.

Article Title: Nepal PM Balen Shah arrives in India for first visit; talks with PM Modi on Monday - top developments
Article Text:
Nepal Prime​ Minister Balendra Shah​​

Long-pending issues likely to figure in talks

Nepali Congress calls for focus on national interest

NEW DELHI: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrived in New Delhi on Sunday for his first official visit to India since taking office, with discussions on energy cooperation, infrastructure, connectivity and bilateral ties expected to feature prominently during his two-day trip. He was received by Union minister Jitin Prasada.Balen Shah with his 34-member delegation is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. The two leaders are also expected to jointly inaugurate energy-related projects and exchange agreements covering various areas of cooperation, Nepal foreign secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said.According to Nepal's Prime Minister's Office, Shah departed for New Delhi on Sunday for the November 22-23 state visit. The PMO said in a post, "Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah departed for New Delhi today on a two-day State Visit to India. He was seen off at the Airport by Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation; Sudan Gurung, Minister for Home Affairs; Jagdish Kharel, Member of the Parliament and Spokesperson of Rastriya Swatantra Party; and senior government officials at the TIA. "During the visit, Shah is also scheduled to call on President Droupadi Murmu, pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat and participate in the Nepal-India Business Forum.A separate business delegation from Nepal is expected to accompany the official delegation.The agenda includes development cooperation, energy ties, rail, road and air connectivity, trade, tourism and infrastructure. The two sides are also expected to explore cooperation in emerging areas such as technology, innovation, start-ups and sports.The Ministry of External Affairs said the visit would provide an opportunity to review the full range of bilateral relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. It described India and Nepal as close neighbours with a wide-ranging partnership rooted in historical, cultural and people-to-people ties.Apart from expanding cooperation, the visit is expected to provide an opportunity to address longstanding differences between the two countries, including the territorial dispute over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura and disagreements over the recruitment of Nepali Gorkhas in the Indian Army.The border dispute has remained unresolved for years. India maintains that the disputed territories are part of Uttarakhand, while the issue continues to be a point of contention between the two neighbours.The two sides could also discuss the report of the Eminent Persons Group (EPG), established jointly by India and Nepal to review bilateral relations. Former adviser to the Nepal prime minister Rajan Bhattarai said the report, prepared by representatives of both countries through consensus, had remained pending for nearly eight years. He expressed hope that it would be taken up during Shah's visit.Bhattarai also said regular high-level engagement was essential to maintaining strong bilateral relations. He pointed to India's position as Nepal's biggest trade partner, largest investor and key development partner, and said Kathmandu would look for continued assistance in post-disaster reconstruction.He identified expanding road and air connectivity, new petroleum pipelines and the possibility of gas pipeline connectivity as other areas for discussion. Climate change, artificial intelligence and advanced technology could also provide new avenues for cooperation, he said."We need very good relations with India, and that is what we expect," Bhattarai said.Ahead of the visit, Nepal's main opposition Nepali Congress urged the government to place the country's national interests at the centre of its engagement with India.Senior vice-president Bishwa Prakash Sharma said the visit should strengthen bilateral ties while ensuring that Nepal's interests were protected.The party identified climate change, tourism, energy, entrepreneurship, sports and trade as areas for cooperation. It also flagged border management, concerns of people living in border areas and challenges faced by Nepali workers in India.The Nepali Congress said relations between the two countries should be based on mutual respect, sovereign equality and national interest. It also urged the government to focus on implementing previous commitments and resolving outstanding issues.Shah's visit follows an invitation from PM Modi after the Rastriya Swatantra Party-led government was formed in March, following the youth-led Gen Z protests that brought down the government of K P Sharma Oli last year.The visit also comes against the backdrop of the diplomatic convention under which newly elected Nepali prime ministers traditionally choose India for their first official bilateral trip. The practice is not binding, however. Oli chose China for his first bilateral visit in 2024.
Article Summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah arrives in New Delhi on Sunday for his first official visit to India since taking office. Shah with his 34-member delegation is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday. The agenda includes development cooperation, energy ties, rail, road and air connectivity, trade, tourism and infrastructure.

Article Title: Watch: Hours after PM Modi inaugurates Nitish Setu, RJD workers tear down NDA banners

Row over the bridge’s name

NEW DELHI: A political showdown erupted on Bihar’s newly inaugurated Nitish Setu on Saturday, with Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) workers pulling down banners and posters put up by the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA), hours after Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the bridge in Vaishali.Videos circulating on social media showed a large group of RJD supporters, tearing down the displays and shouting slogans in support of party supremo Lalu Prasad Yadav and leader of opposition Tejashwi Yadav. Police personnel were seen moving alongside the crowd but appeared unable to control the gathering.The disruption has triggered a fresh exchange between the BJP and RJD, turning the inauguration of a major infrastructure project into a political flashpoint.BJP has accused the RJD of trying to politicise a development project rather than acknowledge its benefits.The bridge, named Nitish Setu, was inaugurated by PM Modi on November 21. The six-lane structure has been built at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore and connects Kacchi Dargah with Bidupur. It is expected to improve connectivity between north and south Bihar and reduce pressure on Mahatma Gandhi Setu.The naming of a bridge in Bihar has triggered a political row, with the Congress and RJD questioning the decision to christen it Nitish Setu instead of naming it after Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.Congress leader Pawan Khera accused the BJP-led Bihar government of hurting Sikh sentiments through the decision. In a post on X, he questioned why a bridge proposed to be named after Guru Gobind Singh was now being named after Nitish Kumar, and whether the move was aimed at pushing the former chief minister out of the political mainstream. "Why is this being done in a way that tramples on the sentiments of the Sikh community?" he asked.Khera also questioned the timing, saying it raised concerns about whether the JD(U) leader was being sidelined while still alive. He shared a Bihar Road Construction Department document containing a note on a non-official resolution moved by RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav regarding the proposed name.Tejashwi had earlier said he moved a private member's resolution in the Bihar Assembly proposing the bridge be named after Guru Gobind Singh. He accused the government of changing its position and said the decision was politically motivated. The Bihar Assembly later said no decision had been taken in the House to name the bridge after Guru Gobind Singh.The controversy has also drawn criticism from AAP leaders in Punjab. Finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema, Assembly speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan and MLA Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal urged the Bihar government to reconsider, saying the bridge's proximity to Takht Sri Patna Sahib made the issue particularly sensitive. Cheema said the government could honour Nitish Kumar in other ways, but going back on a proposal to honour Guru Gobind Singh was unacceptable. Dhaliwal called the decision an insult to Sikh sentiments.Tejashwi also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's inauguration of the bridge, claiming Nitish Kumar had opened it around 17 months earlier and that the project was already in use. He challenged the BJP to identify its contribution to the construction.The inauguration also brought back a familiar election-season image: PM Modi waved his gamcha during the event, recalling his appearance at the BJP office in Patna after the NDA’s victory in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections. The gesture had gone viral at the time, with “Modi Ka Gamcha” trending online after the alliance won 202 of the state’s 243 seats.The bridge inauguration was attended by Bihar governor Lt Gen Syed Ata Hasnain (retd), Union minister Chirag Paswan, chief minister Samrat Choudhary and other dignitaries.
Article Summary: RJD workers tear down NDA banners on Nitish Setu bridge. Row over the bridge’s name has triggered a political flashpoint. BJP has accused the RJD of trying to politicise a development project. Six-lane structure has been built at an estimated cost of Rs 4,280 crore.

Article Title: 'No place for hate in cricket’: Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj

Congress leader rejects Masood’s religious bias charge over Siraj

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Mumtaz Patel has rejected party colleague Imran Masood's allegation of religious discrimination in the selection of the Indian cricket team, saying players have always been picked on the basis of form and suitability rather than religion, caste or region.Patel's remarks came after Masood alleged that fast bowler Mohammed Siraj was left out of India's playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand because of his religious identity. Speaking to news agency ANI, Patel said cricket should remain separate from the communal divisions seen in political discourse."In cricket as a sport, I think there is no space for hate or this religious divide. Firstly, when we talk about Team India, I think the most prominent thing in that is India, and we've always seen cricket in its highest form. I would say that this religious divide, hate divide, is not acceptable," she said.Patel maintained that team selections were based on players' performances and the requirements of a particular tournament."I think cricketers with the best form, best suited in that particular tournament as a team, have always been put together. I doubt I have never seen cricket being divided in the name of states, religion, culture, caste or anything.Let's keep this away," she said.She also criticised political messaging that, in her view, contributed to an atmosphere of division, referring to campaign slogans and remarks by leaders without naming them."At the same time I want to say that let's not create this atmosphere of hate and divide in our country. When you have top leaders on stage talking about people being identified by their clothes, or leaders saying 'batenge toh katenge', it creates a negative atmosphere in the country. Let's keep all this separate. Let's be a united India and especially when it comes to cricket, we are united as Team India," Patel added.Earlier on Saturday, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan had also urged Masood to keep politics and sports separate, saying athletes should not be drawn into political discourse."...I would simply urge Masood-ji to keep politics and sports separate; please, let us not interfere in sports. Sports has its own domain, its own criteria for merit, and every player has their own unique struggle. I strongly believe that while we may engage in political manoeuvring, we should not drag sports or athletes into our political discourse. I find that completely unacceptable..," Ranjan said.The controversy began on Friday after Masood questioned Siraj's omission from the playing eleven, alleging that the decision was linked to his name and religion."It is being said that despite his good performance, he was not given a place in the team. His name is 'Siraj', and that is why he was not given a place. If you are not selecting him despite his good performance, the discrimination is clear," Masood told ANI.On Saturday, Masood cited fast bowler Mohammed Shami and batter Sarfaraz Khan while questioning the selection process."There's Mohammed Shami, there's Sarfaraz, and many others. Selections should be based on performance; if someone is performing well, it shouldn't matter where they come from," he said.Questions over Siraj's omission have also drawn attention to his record in the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. He has taken 43 wickets in 11 matches, according to the information cited in the reports.India selected Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj as its four pacers for the Test, alongside Washington Sundar. The team management cited its bowling combination and the need for additional batting cover.
Article Summary: Congress leader Mumtaz Patel rejects Imran Masood's allegation of religious discrimination in selection of Indian cricket team. Patel says players have always been picked on the basis of form and suitability rather than religion, caste or region. Masood alleged that fast bowler Mohammed Siraj was left out of India's playing eleven for the first Test against New Zealand because of his religious identity.

NEW DELHI: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple in Kerala witnessed a significant rise in the number of devotees on Sunday as the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season began.The state government and temple authorities have put extensive security and administrative measures in place to manage the rush and ensure a smooth pilgrimage, according to new agency ANI.The temple, located in Pathanamthitta district, reopened on November 16, marking the beginning of the annual pilgrimage season.State health minister K Muraleedharan said the government had made arrangements to handle the expected increase in the number of devotees. These include improvements in infrastructure, transport services and other essential facilities.Speaking to the media, Muraleedharan said the renovated road connecting Chalakkayam and Pamba had been inaugurated on Saturday. He added that the Kerala state electricity board (KSEB) had completed electrification work along the route.He also said that Kerala state road transport corporation (KSRTC) buses were operating, while additional private buses had been hired to ferry pilgrims between Nilakkal and Pamba.The minister said the government was satisfied with the preparations and appreciated the cooperation extended by the Devaswom Board. He noted that the number of devotees increases every year and that arrangements had been made to manage the expected heavy rush this season.Meanwhile, the state police have deployed additional personnel at the temple and other important locations to ensure the safety of pilgrims throughout the season.Pathanamthitta superintendent of police and district police chief R Anand said comprehensive security, traffic regulation and surveillance arrangements had been made in coordination with the district administration and local bodies.Speaking to reporters, Anand said police personnel had been deployed at major temples, while parking facilities had been arranged at designated idathavalams (pilgrim resting centres). He assured that the police would work to ensure a safe and smooth pilgrimage.The first phase of the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku season will continue from November 16 to December 27, ending with the Mandala Pooja.After the Mandala period, the shrine will reopen on December 30 for the Makaravilakku festival, scheduled for January 14, 2027. The government, police and Devaswom Board have coordinated their efforts to manage the influx and ensure that pilgrims have access to necessary facilities throughout the season.
Article Summary: The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa Temple in Kerala witnessed a significant rise in the number of devotees on Sunday as the annual Mandala-Makaravilakku pilgrimage season began. BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi, family sources said on Sunday. NEW DELHI: Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah begins his first official visit to India on Sunday, with energy cooperation, infrastructure and connectivity expected to feature prominently in talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alongside efforts to address long-pending differences between the two neighbours.Shah, who is leading a 34-member delegation on the November 22-23 state visit, will be accorded full state honours during his stay, the ministry of external affairs said. He will hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi on Monday, after which the two leaders are expected to jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects and exchange agreements covering different areas of cooperation, Nepal’s foreign secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said.The visit will also include a call on President Droupadi Murmu, a tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat and participation in the Nepal-India Business Forum. A separate business delegation from Nepal is expected to travel alongside the official delegation.The official agenda includes development cooperation, energy ties, rail, road and air connectivity, trade, tourism and infrastructure. The two sides are also expected to explore cooperation in newer areas such as technology, innovation, start-ups and sports.India’s ministry of external affairs said the visit would provide an opportunity to review the full range of bilateral relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. The ministry described India and Nepal as close neighbours with a wide-ranging partnership rooted in historical, cultural and people-to-people ties.Ahead of the visit, former advisor to the Nepal prime minister Rajan Bhattarai said regular high-level engagement was essential to maintaining strong relations and advancing cooperation. He pointed to India’s role as Nepal’s biggest trade partner, largest investor and key development partner, and said Kathmandu would look for continued assistance in post-disaster reconstruction.Bhattarai said the two countries could discuss expanding road and air links, new petroleum pipelines and the possibility of gas pipeline connectivity. Climate change, artificial intelligence and advanced technology could also offer new avenues for cooperation, he said.The visit is also an opportunity for the two sides to discuss differences in bilateral ties, including the territorial dispute over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura, and disagreements over the recruitment of Nepali Gurkhas in the Indian Army.The border dispute has remained unresolved for years. India has consistently maintained that the disputed territories are part of Uttarakhand, while the issue continues to be a point of contention between the two neighbours.Another longstanding matter that could receive attention is the report of the Eminent Persons Group (EPG), set up jointly by India and Nepal to review bilateral relations. Bhattarai said the report, prepared by representatives of both countries through consensus, has remained pending for nearly eight years and expressed hope that it would be taken up during Shah’s visit.“We need very good relations with India, and that is what we expect,” Bhattarai said.The visit has also prompted Nepal’s main opposition Nepali Congress to urge the government to place national interest at the centre of its engagement with India. Senior vice-president Bishwa Prakash Sharma said the trip should strengthen bilateral ties while ensuring that Nepal’s interests were protected.The party said its consultations with experts had identified areas for cooperation including climate change, tourism, energy, entrepreneurship, sports and trade. It also flagged border management, concerns of people living in border areas and challenges faced by Nepali workers in India.The Nepali Congress said the two countries’ relationship should be based on mutual respect, sovereign equality and national interest, and urged the government to focus on implementing past commitments and resolving outstanding issues.Shah’s visit follows the invitation extended by PM Modi after the Rastriya Swatantra Party-led government was formed in March, following the youth-led Gen Z protests that brought down the government of K P Sharma Oli last year.The trip also carries significance against the diplomatic convention that newly elected Nepali prime ministers make India their first official bilateral destination. The practice is not binding, however: Oli chose China for his first bilateral visit in 2024.
Article Summary: Nepal prime minister Balendra Shah begins his first official visit to India on Sunday. Energy cooperation, infrastructure and connectivity are expected to feature prominently in talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The two sides are also expected to explore cooperation in newer areas such as technology, innovation and start-ups.

Article Text:
Kumar's absence from the inauguration of the Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali district

NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) leader Manoj Pandey on Sunday launched a fresh attack on former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar , claiming that the JD(U) had only a few months left and was moving towards its political end.Pandey's remarks came amid a political controversy over Kumar's absence from the inauguration of the Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali district. Speaking to ANI, the JMM leader questioned the repeat inauguration of the project and accused the BJP of taking credit for its construction despite, as he claimed, having no contribution to it.“At the Nitish Setu bridge's inauguration, Nitish Kumar himself was nowhere to be seen. The bridge was there, but Nitish was not. Besides, it had already been inaugurated in the past. What is the intention behind doing it again? What kind of 'development' concept is this? It’s beyond comprehension. Furthermore, as far as we are aware, the Central Government had no role in this bridge—yet, they showed up to take the credit. ....Nitish Kumar is finished. The JD(U) now has only a few months left. Based on the political developments that have unfolded, it is clear that the JD(U) is heading towards its end...”Pandey told ANI.The remarks follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi 's inauguration of the Rs 4,280-crore bridge over the Ganga on November 21. Kumar was not present at the main ceremony in Vaishali, which was attended by Modi, Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary and Union Minister Chirag Paswan.The event also drew criticism from RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, who questioned the decision to name the bridge after a living political leader. Speaking to ANI, Yadav argued that memorials were traditionally associated with departed figures and suggested that the naming indicated Kumar was “politically finished”.Yadav further claimed that Kumar had already inaugurated the bridge earlier and alleged that the Centre had not funded the project.Despite missing the inauguration ceremony, Kumar met Modi at Patna airport before the Prime Minister's visit to Vaishali. Modi later shared a post on X, saying, “It was a delight to meet Nitish Kumar Ji at Patna airport.”
Article Summary: Pandey's remarks come amid a political controversy over Kumar's absence from the inauguration of the Nitish Setu bridge in Vaishali district. The JMM leader accused the BJP of taking credit for its construction despite, as he claimed, having no contribution to it.
